question: how many decision bars does the 11-11 trim (gap_k) survive before the schedule climbs back over the level it cut from?

derived_erasure.basis: slack / observed step; an expectation on the step law, not a simulation

sentence: No historical decision bar dropped k by as much as the 6.72pp trim (largest drop in 33 same-window steps was 0.61pp), so the record never tested whether such a cut holds; on the observed step law it takes about 10 upward steps of 0.69pp (mean) / 22 steps of 0.31pp (median) to walk the slack back -- but the largest single upward step (6.76pp over 19 up-steps) exceeds the whole cut, so the trim can be erased in one decision bar; walking it back at the mean step takes 10 bars. Nothing in the schedule remembers the floor, so it has to be re-applied every decision bar.
